newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher as selling dries up.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mostly higher as selling dries up.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled mostly higher as fund selling failed to show up after having pressured values Monday, traders said.

"All the selling just kind of dried up. I think part of it was a correction -- we beat the May up pretty hard yesterday and I think people wanted to bring it back in line with the other markets," a trader said.

KCBT wheat also drew support from outside markets such as CBOT wheat, which climbed on fund-related buying, and from CBOT soybeans. Wheat was also lifted by the ongoing risk of spring wheat planting delays in the northern Plains from excessive wet conditions, traders said.
KCBT July, which had been pressured early by a general improvement in the condition of the HRW wheat crop, turned higher in the session's second half.
Monday's weekly state crop reports rated more than 80 percent of the wheat in Kansas and Oklahoma as good to excellent.
KCBT wheat settled three cents per bushel lower to 3-1/4 cents higher, with May up 3-1/4 cents at $4.08-3/4. July gained 1-1/4 cents to close at $3.79.
Wolcott Lincoln and Benson-Quinn each sold at least one million July bushels, traders said.
Also, LFG bought one million July and Prudential bought 800,000 May, sources said.
